title: Fix the Shallow Copy Side Effect
description: The program should duplicate a list of lists so that modifying the copy never affects the original. Fix the bug.
buggyCode:
import copy

original = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
duplicate = copy.copy(original)
duplicate[0][0] = 99
print(original[0][0])
expectedBehavior: The program should print 1 — modifying the duplicate should never affect the original.
actualProblem: copy.copy() performs a shallow copy: it copies the outer list, but the inner lists are still shared references between original and duplicate. Mutating duplicate[0][0] therefore also changes original[0][0].
correctedCode:
import copy

original = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
duplicate = copy.deepcopy(original)
duplicate[0][0] = 99
print(original[0][0])
explanation: To fully separate nested (mutable) structures so changes to one don't affect the other, use copy.deepcopy(), which recursively copies every nested object instead of just the outermost container.
